## Ex 2

Write code that reads in all the JSON files in the `objects` folder and returns a tibble with the following columns: 
'id','accession_number','title','artist','classification','continent','country','dated','life_date','department','culture','nationality','room','style','medium','dimension','description','object_name'

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(jsonlite)
library(ggplot2)
```


```{r eval = FALSE}
path <- "../homework-7-shufubianyibo/data/raw/objects"
files <- dir(path, pattern = "*.json",recursive = TRUE)
file_paths <- file.path(path,files)[1:5000]
# Write a function called read_json_file that reads in one JSON File and flattens it to a data frame
# Note: Use try() to silently handle errors in reading in the JSON file; if error occurs, return NULL
# If any values are missing of the columns of interest, replace the NULL with NA
# Return a data frame with 1 row and only the following columns: 'id','accession_number','title','artist','classification','continent','country','dated','life_date','department','culture','nationality','room','style','medium','dimension','description','object_name'

nullToNA <- function(x){
  if(is.null(x)){
    x <- NA
  }
  x
}

read_json_file <- function(file_path){
  res <- try(fromJSON(file_path, flatten = TRUE), silent = TRUE)
  target_columns <- c('id', 'accession_number', 'title', 'artist', 'classification',
                      'continent', 'country', 'dated', 'life_date', 'department',
                      'culture', 'nationality', 'room', 'style', 'medium',
                      'dimension', 'description', 'object_name')
  if(inherits(res, "try-error")){
    return(NULL)
  }
  output <- setNames(vector("list", length(target_columns)), target_columns)
  for (col in target_columns) {
    if (col %in% names(res)) {
      value <- res[[col]]
      if (is.null(value)) {
        output[[col]] <- NA
      } else {
        output[[col]] <- value
      }
    } else {
      output[[col]] <- NA 
    }
  }
  return(as_tibble(output))
}


# Use map() to read in all file_paths and list_rbind() to combine them into a tibble/data frame

mia_collection <- 
  list_rbind(map(file_paths,read_json_file))
  


  
  
dim(mia_collection)
head(mia_collection)
```

## Ex 4

Explore the `continent` variable. Create a "clean" version of the variable called `continent_clean` such that each object has 1 value from the following: "Europe", "Africa", "North America", "Asia", "South America", "Antarctica", "Oceania", "Unknown Continent". As you clean the variable, state your assumptions explicitly so that someone could replicate your work based on your words. 

> Assumptions: First set a vector including: "Europe", "Africa", "North America", "Asia", "South America", "Antarctica", "Oceania". Set a function to check whether the input value equals to any value in the vector, if not set the value to "Unknown Continent", else do nothing. At last, use map to loop over every value in the column with the function.
> 

```{r}
mia_collection <- read.csv("data/clean/mia_collection.csv")
continent_names<- c("Europe", "Africa", "North America", "Asia", "South America", "Antarctica", "Oceania")

check_continent_name <- function(value) {
  if (!value %in% continent_names || is.na(value)) {
    value <- "Unknown Continent"
  }
  return(value)
}


mia_collection <- mia_collection %>%
  mutate(continent_clean = map_chr(as.character(continent), check_continent_name))








# Don't erase the code below; this will show your final work
mia_collection %>% 
  count(continent_clean)

unique(mia_collection$continent_clean)
```


## Ex 5

Make a visualization that looks at the relationship between `department` and `continent_clean`.

```{r}
ggplot(mia_collection, aes(x = department, fill = continent_clean)) +
    geom_bar(position = "stack") + 
    labs(
      title = "Distribution of Art Objects by Continent within Mia Departments",
      x = "Department",
      y = "Number of Objects",
      fill = "Continent (Cleaned)" 
    )+
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 65, hjust = 1, vjust = 1))
```
